{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0123PqKj8gWH8Zx9HtzVcn4G","type":"tool_result","content":"<persisted-output>\nOutput too large (32.7KB). Full output saved to: /home/barlo/.drydock/claude-home/projects/-mnt-c-Users-barlo-projects-drydock-uat-FxRates-runs-20261027-152427-build-FxRates/cb08b2e3-109d-4e7e-b122-fe6bd5fd3439/tool-results/bp9vq4qph.txt\n\nPreview (first 2KB):\n=== fxrates\n#!/bin/sh\n# fxrates — application launcher. Activates .venv when present and hands the arguments to the\n# cli package. Database access goes through the shipped `persistence` package only.\n\"\"\"\n=== fxrates_app/config.py\n\"\"\"Database location: one place decides which store the application opens.\n\nResolution order: DATABASE_URL, then DATABASE_PATH, then data/app.db. It performs no database access and reads no file.\nRates keep their published text; they are never converted to a number.\n\"\"\"\n\n...\n</persisted-output>","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"cb08b2e3-109d-4e7e-b122-fe6bd5fd3439","uuid":"dfd119d2-df1c-4cfc-8cea-9ee54142cb42","timestamp":"2026-10-27T16:07:49.733Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"=== fxrates\n#!/bin/sh\n# fxrates — application launcher. Activates .venv when present and hands the arguments to the\n# cli package. It holds no command logic; every command is dispatched by cli.main.\nROOT=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\"\ncd \"$ROOT\"\nif [ -f \"$ROOT/.venv/bin/activate\" ]; then\n    . \"$ROOT/.venv/bin/activate\"\nfi\nexec python -m cli \"$@\"\n=== fxrates_app/__init__.py\n\"\"\"FxRates application package.\n\nApplication modules (config, ecb, fetch, rates, history, convert, commands) are added by later\nbuild blocks. Database access goes through the shipped `persistence` package only.\n\"\"\"\n=== fxrates_app/config.py\n\"\"\"Database location: one place decides which store the application opens.\n\nResolution order: DATABASE_URL, then DATABASE_PATH, then data/app.db. The environment is read at\ncall time. Application code opens the store only through `persistence.open_database`.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\n\nfrom persistence import Database, open_database\n\nDEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH = \"data/app.db\"\nSQLITE_PREFIX = \"sqlite://\"\n\n\ndef database_path() -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the database location from the environment, falling back to data/app.db.\"\"\"\n    url = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_URL\", \"\")\n    if url.startswith(SQLITE_PREFIX):\n        url = url[len(SQLITE_PREFIX):]\n    if url:\n        return url\n    path = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_PATH\", \"\")\n    if path:\n        return path\n    return DEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH\n\n\ndef open_store() -> Database:\n    \"\"\"Open the store named by `database_path()` through the persistence library.\"\"\"\n    return open_database(database_path())\n=== fxrates_app/ecb.py\n\"\"\"ECB history file validation: one pure function checks a whole file before any write.\n\n`parse_history` reads the text of an ECB euro reference rate history file and returns every\nnon-N/A value as (date, currency, rate_text). It performs no database access and reads no file.\nRates keep their published text; they are never converted to a number.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport datetime\nimport io\nimport re\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nFIRST_HEADER_FIELD = \"Date\"\nNOT_AVAILABLE = \"N/A\"\n\n_DATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\")\n_CURRENCY_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Z]{3}\")\n_RATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?\")\n\n\nclass RejectedFile(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised when an ECB history file violates the format; no rate from it may be written.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef parse_history(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Validate the whole file and return (date, currency, rate_text) for every non-N/A value.\n\n    Raises RejectedFile on the first violation found anywhere in the file.\n    \"\"\"\n    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(text)))\n    if not rows:\n        raise RejectedFile(\"file has no header\")\n\n    header = _drop_trailing_comma(rows[0])\n    if not header or header[0] != FIRST_HEADER_FIELD:\n        raise RejectedFile(\"header must begin with Date\")\n    currencies = header[1:]\n    for code in currencies:\n        if not _CURRENCY_PATTERN.fullmatch(code):\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"malformed currency code in header: {code!r}\")\n    if len(set(currencies)) != len(currencies):\n        raise RejectedFile(\"currency code repeated in header\")\n\n    rates: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n    seen_dates: set[str] = set()\n    for line_number, raw in enumerate(rows[1:], start=2):\n        fields = _drop_trailing_comma(raw)\n        if len(fields) != len(header):\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has {len(fields)} fields, expected {len(header)}\")\n\n        date_text = fields[0]\n        _check_date(date_text, line_number)\n        if date_text in seen_dates:\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} repeats date {date_text}\")\n        seen_dates.add(date_text)\n\n        for code, value in zip(currencies, fields[1:]):\n            if value == NOT_AVAILABLE:\n                continue\n            _check_rate(value, line_number)\n            rates.append((date_text, code, value))\n\n    return rates\n\n\ndef _drop_trailing_comma(fields: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The ECB writes a trailing comma on each line; the resulting empty last field is ignored.\"\"\"\n    if fields and fields[-1] == \"\":\n        return fields[:-1]\n    return fields\n\n\ndef _check_date(text: str, line_number: int) -> None:\n    if not _DATE_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a malformed date: {text!r}\")\n    try:\n        datetime.date.fromisoformat(text)\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has an impossible date: {text!r}\") from error\n\n\ndef _check_rate(text: str, line_number: int) -> None:\n    if not _RATE_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a malformed rate: {text!r}\")\n    if Decimal(text) == 0:\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a zero rate: {text!r}\")\n=== cli/__init__.py\n\"\"\"Command-line package: `main(argv) -> int` dispatches to handlers registered by command stories.\"\"\"\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import main, register_command\nfrom cli import init_command  # noqa: F401  registers the `init` handler at import\nfrom cli import load_command  # noqa: F401  registers the `load` handler at import\n\n__all__ = [\"main\", \"register_command\"]\n=== cli/__main__.py\n\"\"\"Lets `python -m cli` run the dispatcher; the launcher `fxrates` uses this form.\"\"\"\n\nimport sys\n\nfrom cli import main\n\nsys.exit(main())\n=== cli/dispatcher.py\n\"\"\"Command registry and dispatch.\n\nCommand stories register a handler under a command name at import time. `main` hands the\nremaining arguments to the handler and returns the handler's exit code.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom cli import usage\n\nUSAGE_ERROR = 2\n\n_handlers: dict[str, Callable[[list[str]], int]] = {}\n\n\ndef register_command(name: str, handler: Callable[[list[str]], int]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Map a command name to its handler; registering a name again replaces the handler.\"\"\"\n    _handlers[name] = handler\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Validate `argv`, dispatch `argv[0]` to its registered handler, and return the exit code.\"\"\"\n    args = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)\n    try:\n        usage.validate(args, _handlers)\n    except usage.UsageError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return USAGE_ERROR\n    handler = _handlers.get(args[0])\n    if handler is None:\n        print(f\"error: command not available in this build: {args[0]}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return USAGE_ERROR\n    return handler(args[1:])\n=== cli/init_command.py\n\"\"\"The `init` command: empty the rates store, print nothing, exit 0.\n\nThe schema is provisioned by the DATABASE step, so init never runs DDL or opens a driver. It\nremoves every stored rate through the declared `rates.delete_from_date` operation, passing a date\nearlier than any publication, and leaves the table in place with no rows.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\n\nEARLIEST_DATE = \"0000-01-01\"\n\n\ndef init(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Remove every stored rate and return 0. The argument list is validated before dispatch.\"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        db.rates.delete_from_date(from_date=EARLIEST_DATE)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n    return 0\n\n\nregister_command(\"init\", init)\n=== cli/load_command.py\n\"\"\"The `load` command: validate an ECB history file, store its rates, report the counts.\n\n`parse_history` checks the whole file before the first write, so a rejected file exits 3 and stores\nnothing. A file that cannot be opened or decoded exits 1 before any parsing or store access. Each rate is then written through the declared `rates.replace_rate` operation, which\nreplaces a rate already stored for the same date and currency, so loading a file twice leaves the\ndatabase unchanged.\n\nThe persistence library exposes no transaction operation, so each replace commits on its own. The\nvalidation above is what keeps a rejected file from changing anything; a store failure part way\nthrough a valid file is not rolled back.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sys\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import RejectedFile, parse_history\n\nOPERATIONAL_FAILURE = 1\nREJECTED = 3\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\n\n\ndef load(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Load the file named in `rest[0]` and return the exit code. The argument list is pre-validated.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0\n    try:\n        with open(rest[0], encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\") as handle:\n            text = handle.read()\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot read {rest[0]}: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        rates = parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile as error:\n        print(f\"error: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return REJECTED\n\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        for date, currency, rate in rates:\n            db.rates.replace_rate(date=date, currency=currency, rate=rate)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n\n    dates = {date for date, _, _ in rates}\n    print(\"dates,rates\")\n    print(f\"{len(dates)},{len(rates)}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nregister_command(\"load\", load)\n=== cli/testing.py\n\"\"\"In-process test helper: runs the dispatcher without spawning a process.\"\"\"\n\nimport contextlib\nimport io\n\nfrom cli import main\n\n\ndef cli_runner(*args: str) -> tuple[int, str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Return (exit_code, stdout, stderr) for the given arguments.\"\"\"\n    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()\n    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):\n        code = main(list(args))\n    return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()\n=== cli/usage.py\n\"\"\"Argument validation for the fxrates command line.\n\n`validate` runs before dispatch and rejects a malformed invocation with `UsageError`, so the caller\ncan exit 2 with empty stdout and one stderr line. It never opens a database or binds a socket.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Collection\n\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\nPORT_FLAG = \"--port\"\nPORT_MIN = 1\nPORT_MAX = 65535\n\n# Exact positional argument counts for the commands whose stories are in the blueprint table.\n_ARITY: dict[str, int] = {\"init\": 0, \"load\": 1, \"fetch\": 0}\n_SERVE = \"serve\"\n\n\nclass UsageError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"A malformed invocation. The message is one line; its wording is not part of the contract.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef validate(argv: list[str], registered: Collection[str] = ()) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Raise UsageError unless `argv` names a known command with well-formed arguments.\n\n    `registered` holds the names of commands with a handler. A command outside the table above\n    and outside `registered` is a usage error; a registered command outside the table is not\n    arity-checked.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not argv:\n        raise UsageError(\"no command given; usage: fxrates <command> [arguments...]\")\n    command, rest = argv[0], list(argv[1:])\n    if command == _SERVE:\n        _validate_serve(rest)\n    elif command in _ARITY:\n        _validate_arity(command, rest)\n    elif command not in registered:\n        raise UsageError(f\"unknown command: {command}\")\n\n\ndef _validate_arity(command: str, rest: list[str]) -> None:\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return\n    expected = _ARITY[command]\n    if len(rest) != expected:\n        raise UsageError(f\"{command} takes {expected} argument(s), got {len(rest)}\")\n\n\ndef _validate_serve(rest: list[str]) -> None:\n    if not rest or rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return\n    if len(rest) != 2 or rest[0] != PORT_FLAG:\n        raise UsageError(f\"serve takes an optional {PORT_FLAG} <n>\")\n    _validate_port(rest[1])\n\n\ndef _validate_port(value: str) -> None:\n    if not re.fullmatch(r\"[0-9]+\", value) or not PORT_MIN <= int(value) <= PORT_MAX:\n        raise UsageError(f\"{PORT_FLAG} must be an integer from {PORT_MIN} to {PORT_MAX}, got {value!r}\")\n=== app_server/__init__.py\n\"\"\"HTTP application package: the FastAPI factory, the shared router registry, and the test client.\"\"\"\n=== app_server/main.py\n\"\"\"FastAPI application factory and the module-level app for `uvicorn app_server.main:app`.\"\"\"\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI\n\nfrom app_server import routes\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    \"\"\"Build a new FastAPI application that includes the shared router.\"\"\"\n    application = FastAPI()\n    application.include_router(routes.router)\n    return application\n\n\napp = create_app()\n=== app_server/routes.py\n\"\"\"Shared router registry. Feature stories attach their routes here; static routes go first.\"\"\"\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter\n\nrouter = APIRouter()\n=== app_server/testing.py\n\"\"\"In-process test client for the application; used by acceptance and the pytest suite.\"\"\"\n\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app_server.main import create_app\n\n\ndef web_client() -> TestClient:\n    \"\"\"Return a TestClient wrapping a new application instance.\"\"\"\n    return TestClient(create_app())\n=== persistence/testing.py\n\"\"\"Generated fixtures over the configured, already provisioned application store.\"\"\"\n\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom .schema import open_database\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef committed_session():\n    \"\"\"Use normal autocommit for project tests; under the acceptance harness, its transaction.\"\"\"\n    configured = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_URL\") or os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_PATH\") or \"data/app.db\"\n    if not configured.startswith((\"postgres://\", \"postgresql://\")):\n        if not Path(configured.split(\"://\", 1)[-1]).is_file():\n            raise RuntimeError(\"persistence store missing; rebuild the DATABASE step\")\n    database = open_database(configured)\n    try:\n        yield database\n    finally:\n        database.close()\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef db_session():\n    \"\"\"Share this connection with the feature; always roll back, never provision schema.\n\n    Under the acceptance harness the rollback is the harness's, at the end of the criterion, so\n    a request made after this block still sees the setup.\n    \"\"\"\n    with committed_session() as database:\n        with database.rollback_session():\n            yield database\n=== persistence/__init__.py\n\"\"\"Persistence for this Target. Shipped engines plus the schema generated from DATABASE.md.\"\"\"\n\nfrom .db import Database, PersistenceError, UnknownOperation\nfrom .schema import SCHEMA, open_database\n\n__all__ = [\"Database\", \"PersistenceError\", \"SCHEMA\", \"UnknownOperation\", \"open_database\"]\n=== bin/test.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# CommandCenter Operation\n# Name: Run Test Suite\n# Type: batch\n\n# --- Standard Preamble ---\nset -eu\nSCRIPT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\"\nPROJECT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$SCRIPT_DIR/..\" && pwd)\"\nLOG_DIR=\"$PROJECT_DIR/data/logs\"\nmkdir -p \"$LOG_DIR\"\n\nTIMESTAMP=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S')\nSCRIPT_NAME=$(basename \"$0\" .sh)\nLOG_FILE=\"$LOG_DIR/${SCRIPT_NAME}_${TIMESTAMP}.log\"\n\necho \"=== $SCRIPT_NAME started at $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') ===\" | tee \"$LOG_FILE\"\necho \"Arguments: $*\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\necho \"Working dir: $PROJECT_DIR\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\necho \"---\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\n\ncd \"$PROJECT_DIR\"\n\nif [ ! -f \".venv/bin/activate\" ]; then\n    echo \"Environment missing: run 'uv sync' in $PROJECT_DIR first\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# --- Run the declared test_command: pytest -q ---\n# Calls the environment's pytest directly; sourcing activate trips `set -u`. Output is captured\n# in full so the exit status of pytest is kept (a pipe would hide it).\nset +e\n\"$PROJECT_DIR/.venv/bin/pytest\" -q >\"$LOG_FILE.pytest\" 2>&1\nSTATUS=$?\nset -e\ncat \"$LOG_FILE.pytest\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\nrm -f \"$LOG_FILE.pytest\"\n\necho \"=== $SCRIPT_NAME finished at $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') with status $STATUS ===\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\nexit \"$STATUS\"\n=== pyproject.toml\n[project]\nname = \"fxrates\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.11\"\ndependencies = [\n    \"fastapi>=0.162.0\",\n    \"httpx2>=2.16.0\",\n    \"uvicorn>=0.54.0\",\n]\n\n[dependency-groups]\ndev = [\n    \"pytest>=9.1.1\",\n]\n\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\ntestpaths = [\"tests\"]\npythonpath = [\".\"]\n=== tests/conftest.py\n\"\"\"Shared pytest fixtures for the FxRates suite.\n\nTests never open a network connection. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\n#\n# Runs ./fxrates against a fresh database: loads the supplied ECB files from the command line,\n# starts `./fxrates serve` on a free local port, and compares every command's exit code and\n# standard output, and every HTTP response's status and JSON body, with the known answer below.\n# JSON bodies are compared as values, so key order and whitespace do not matter. Standard error\n# and error-response bodies are never compared. No network beyond 127.0.0.1 is used.\n#\n#   sh sources/run.sh               from the application root (how `drydock uat` runs it)\n#   sh uat/FxRates/bin/run.sh APP   from anywhere, grading the application root APP\n#\n# Exit 0 only when every check passes.\nset -u\n\nHERE=$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\nAPP=$(cd \"${1:-.}\" && pwd)\nif [ -f \"$HERE/eurofxref-hist_2025-01.csv\" ]; then DATA=$HERE; else DATA=$(cd \"$HERE/../sources\" && pwd); fi\nWORK=$(mktemp -d)\nBIN=\"$APP/fxrates\"\nDATABASE_URL=\"$WORK/fxrates.db\"\nexport DATABASE_URL\nSERVER=\"\"\nPORT=$(python3 -c 'import socket; s = socket.socket(); s.bind((\"127.0.0.1\", 0)); print(s.getsockname()[1])')\nBASE=\"http://127.0.0.1:$PORT\"\n\nstop_server() {\n    if [ -n \"$SERVER\" ]; then\n        pkill -TERM -P \"$SERVER\" 2>/dev/null\n        kill -TERM \"$SERVER\" 2>/dev/null\n        wait \"$SERVER\" 2>/dev/null\n        SERVER=\"\"\n    fi\n}\ntrap 'stop_server; rm -rf \"$WORK\"' EXIT\ntrap 'exit 1' INT TERM\n\nif [ ! -x \"$BIN\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: no executable ./fxrates at the application root $APP.\" >&2\n    echo \"The deliverable is an executable named fxrates at the application root.\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nPASSED=0\nFAILED=0\n\npass() { PASSED=$((PASSED + 1)); echo \"PASS $1\"; }\nfail() { FAILED=$((FAILED + 1)); echo \"FAIL $1\"; }\n\n# check <id> <expected exit> <fxrates args...>  — expected standard output on stdin.\ncheck() {\n    id=$1\n    want_rc=$2\n    shift 2\n    cat > \"$WORK/want\"\n    (cd \"$APP\" && \"$BIN\" \"$@\") > \"$WORK/got\" 2> \"$WORK/err\" < /dev/null\n    rc=$?\n    if [ \"$rc\" -eq \"$want_rc\" ] && cmp -s \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\"; then\n        pass \"$id: fxrates $*\"\n    else\n        fail \"$id: fxrates $*\"\n        echo \"  exit: expected $want_rc, got $rc\"\n        diff \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\" | sed 's/^/  /'\n        sed 's/^/  stderr: /' \"$WORK/err\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# http <id> <expected status> <path>  — expected JSON body on stdin (compared only for 200).\nhttp() {\n    id=$1\n    want_status=$2\n    path=$3\n    cat > \"$WORK/want\"\n    if python3 - \"$BASE$path\" \"$want_status\" \"$WORK/want\" > \"$WORK/got\" 2>&1 <<'PY'\nimport json, sys, urllib.error, urllib.request\nurl, want, want_file = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3]\ntry:\n    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=15) as r:\n        status, body = r.status, r.read()\nexcept urllib.error.HTTPError as e:\n---\nDate,USD,JPY,GBP,CHF,SEK,CAD,AUD,CNY,HRK,\n2025-01-31,1.0393,160.99,0.83608,0.9449,11.474,1.5035,1.6702,7.5363,N/A,\n2025-01-30,1.0403,160.32,0.83685,0.9441,11.47,1.4997,1.6705,7.5436,N/A,\n---\ntotal 44\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo  512 Oct 27 11:41 .\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo  512 Oct 27 11:40 ..\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo 4155 Oct 27 11:40 activate\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo 2728 Oct 27 11:40 activate.bat\n# Runtime\ndata/\n*.db\n*.log\n\n# Environment\n.env\n.venv/\nvenv/\n\n# Python\n__pycache__/\n*.pyc\n*.egg-info/\ndist/\nbuild/\n.pytest_cache/\n\n# OS\n.DS_Store\nThumbs.db","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01EF7FqJkYjYKCmtmYDi57HY","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01J93pPRR5Lf7ypPCeyUrVFf","type":"tool_result","content":"=== fxrates_app/ecb.py\n\"\"\"ECB history file validation: one pure function checks a whole file before any write.\n\n`parse_history` reads the text of an ECB euro reference rate history file and returns every\nnon-N/A value as (date, currency, rate_text). It performs no database access and reads no file.\nRates keep their published text; they are never converted to a number.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport datetime\nimport io\nimport re\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nFIRST_HEADER_FIELD = \"Date\"\nNOT_AVAILABLE = \"N/A\"\n\n_DATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\")\n_CURRENCY_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Z]{3}\")\n_RATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?\")\n\n\nclass RejectedFile(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised when an ECB history file violates the format; no rate from it may be written.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef parse_history(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Validate the whole file and return (date, currency, rate_text) for every non-N/A value.\n\n    Raises RejectedFile on the first violation found anywhere in the file.\n    \"\"\"\n    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(text)))\n    if not rows:\n        raise RejectedFile(\"file has no header\")\n\n    header = _drop_trailing_comma(rows[0])\n    if not header or header[0] != FIRST_HEADER_FIELD:\n        raise RejectedFile(\"header must begin with Date\")\n    currencies = header[1:]\n    for code in currencies:\n        if not _CURRENCY_PATTERN.fullmatch(code):\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"malformed currency code in header: {code!r}\")\n    if len(set(currencies)) != len(currencies):\n        raise RejectedFile(\"currency code repeated in header\")\n\n    rates: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n    seen_dates: set[str] = set()\n    for line_number, raw in enumerate(rows[1:], start=2):\n        fields = _drop_trailing_comma(raw)\n        if len(fields) != len(header):\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has {len(fields)} fields, expected {len(header)}\")\n\n        date_text = fields[0]\n        _check_date(date_text, line_number)\n        if date_text in seen_dates:\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} repeats date {date_text}\")\n        seen_dates.add(date_text)\n\n        for code, value in zip(currencies, fields[1:]):\n            if value == NOT_AVAILABLE:\n                continue\n            _check_rate(value, line_number)\n            rates.append((date_text, code, value))\n\n    return rates\n\n\ndef _drop_trailing_comma(fields: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The ECB writes a trailing comma on each line; the resulting empty last field is ignored.\"\"\"\n    if fields and fields[-1] == \"\":\n        return fields[:-1]\n    return fields\n\n\ndef _check_date(text: str, line_number: int) -> None:\n    if not _DATE_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a malformed date: {text!r}\")\n    try:\n        datetime.date.fromisoformat(text)\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has an impossible date: {text!r}\") from error\n\n\ndef _check_rate(text: str, line_number: int) -> None:\n    if not _RATE_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a malformed rate: {text!r}\")\n    if Decimal(text) == 0:\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a zero rate: {text!r}\")\n=== cli/__init__.py\n\"\"\"Command-line package: `main(argv) -> int` dispatches to handlers registered by command stories.\"\"\"\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import main, register_command\nfrom cli import init_command  # noqa: F401  registers the `init` handler at import\nfrom cli import load_command  # noqa: F401  registers the `load` handler at import\n\n__all__ = [\"main\", \"register_command\"]\n=== cli/__main__.py\n\"\"\"Lets `python -m cli` run the dispatcher; the launcher `fxrates` uses this form.\"\"\"\n\nimport sys\n\nfrom cli import main\n\nsys.exit(main())\n=== cli/dispatcher.py\n\"\"\"Command registry and dispatch.\n\nCommand stories register a handler under a command name at import time. `main` hands the\nremaining arguments to the handler and returns the handler's exit code.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom cli import usage\n\nUSAGE_ERROR = 2\n\n_handlers: dict[str, Callable[[list[str]], int]] = {}\n\n\ndef register_command(name: str, handler: Callable[[list[str]], int]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Map a command name to its handler; registering a name again replaces the handler.\"\"\"\n    _handlers[name] = handler\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Validate `argv`, dispatch `argv[0]` to its registered handler, and return the exit code.\"\"\"\n    args = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)\n    try:\n        usage.validate(args, _handlers)\n    except usage.UsageError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return USAGE_ERROR\n    handler = _handlers.get(args[0])\n    if handler is None:\n        print(f\"error: command not available in this build: {args[0]}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return USAGE_ERROR\n    return handler(args[1:])\n=== cli/load_command.py\n\"\"\"The `load` command: validate an ECB history file, store its rates, report the counts.\n\n`parse_history` checks the whole file before the first write, so a rejected file exits 3 and stores\nnothing. A file that cannot be opened or decoded exits 1 before any parsing or store access. Each rate is then written through the declared `rates.replace_rate` operation, which\nreplaces a rate already stored for the same date and currency, so loading a file twice leaves the\ndatabase unchanged.\n\nThe persistence library exposes no transaction operation, so each replace commits on its own. The\nvalidation above is what keeps a rejected file from changing anything; a store failure part way\nthrough a valid file is not rolled back.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sys\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import RejectedFile, parse_history\n\nOPERATIONAL_FAILURE = 1\nREJECTED = 3\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\n\n\ndef load(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Load the file named in `rest[0]` and return the exit code. The argument list is pre-validated.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0\n    try:\n        with open(rest[0], encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\") as handle:\n            text = handle.read()\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot read {rest[0]}: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        rates = parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile as error:\n        print(f\"error: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return REJECTED\n\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        for date, currency, rate in rates:\n            db.rates.replace_rate(date=date, currency=currency, rate=rate)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n\n    dates = {date for date, _, _ in rates}\n    print(\"dates,rates\")\n    print(f\"{len(dates)},{len(rates)}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nregister_command(\"load\", load)\n=== cli/usage.py\n\"\"\"Argument validation for the fxrates command line.\n\n`validate` runs before dispatch and rejects a malformed invocation with `UsageError`, so the caller\ncan exit 2 with empty stdout and one stderr line. It never opens a database or binds a socket.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Collection\n\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\nPORT_FLAG = \"--port\"\nPORT_MIN = 1\nPORT_MAX = 65535\n\n# Exact positional argument counts for the commands whose stories are in the blueprint table.\n_ARITY: dict[str, int] = {\"init\": 0, \"load\": 1, \"fetch\": 0}\n_SERVE = \"serve\"\n\n\nclass UsageError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"A malformed invocation. The message is one line; its wording is not part of the contract.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef validate(argv: list[str], registered: Collection[str] = ()) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Raise UsageError unless `argv` names a known command with well-formed arguments.\n\n    `registered` holds the names of commands with a handler. It performs no database access and reads no file.\nRates keep their published text; they are never converted to a number.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport datetime\nimport io\nimport re\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nFIRST_HEADER_FIELD = \"Date\"\nNOT_AVAILABLE = \"N/A\"\n\n_DATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\")\n_CURRENCY_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Z]{3}\")\n_RATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?\")\n\n\nclass RejectedFile(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised when an ECB history file violates the format; no rate from it may be written.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef parse_history(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Validate the whole file and return (date, currency, rate_text) for every non-N/A value.\n\n    Raises RejectedFile on the first violation found anywhere in the file.\n    \"\"\"\n    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(text)))\n    if not rows:\n        raise RejectedFile(\"file has no header\")\n\n    header = _drop_trailing_comma(rows[0])\n    if not header or header[0] != FIRST_HEADER_FIELD:\n        raise RejectedFile(\"header must begin with Date\")\n    currencies = header[1:]\n    for code in currencies:\n        if not _CURRENCY_PATTERN.fullmatch(code):\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"malformed currency code in header: {code!r}\")\n    if len(set(currencies)) != len(currencies):\n        raise RejectedFile(\"currency code repeated in header\")\n\n    rates: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n    seen_dates: set[str] = set()\n    for line_number, raw in enumerate(rows[1:], start=2):\n        fields = _drop_trailing_comma(raw)\n        if len(fields) != len(header):\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has {len(fields)} fields, expected {len(header)}\")\n\n        date_text = fields[0]\n        _check_date(date_text, line_number)\n        if date_text in seen_dates:\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} repeats date {date_text}\")\n        seen_dates.add(date_text)\n\n        for code, value in zip(currencies, fields[1:]):\n            if value == NOT_AVAILABLE:\n                continue\n            _check_rate(value, line_number)\n            rates.append((date_text, code, value))\n\n    return rates\n\n\ndef _drop_trailing_comma(fields: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The ECB writes a trailing comma on each line; registering a name again replaces the handler.\"\"\"\n    _handlers[name] = handler\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Validate `argv`, dispatch `argv[0]` to its registered handler, and return the exit code.\"\"\"\n    args = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)\n    try:\n        usage.validate(args, _handlers)\n    except usage.UsageError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return USAGE_ERROR\n    handler = _handlers.get(args[0])\n    if handler is None:\n        print(f\"error: command not available in this build: {args[0]}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return USAGE_ERROR\n    return handler(args[1:])\n=== cli/load_command.py\n\"\"\"The `load` command: validate an ECB history file, store its rates, report the counts.\n\n`parse_history` checks the whole file before the first write, so a rejected file exits 3 and stores\nnothing. Each rate is then written through the declared `rates.replace_rate` operation, which\nreplaces a rate already stored for the same date and currency, so loading a file twice leaves the\ndatabase unchanged.\n\nThe persistence library exposes no transaction operation, so each replace commits on its own. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0196m9oZpbQCzQ8oF8hagain","type":"tool_result","content":"=== tests/conftest.py\n\"\"\"Shared pytest fixtures for the FxRates suite.\n\nTests never open a network connection. Any attempt to connect a socket fails the test, so an\naccidental download cannot slip through a suite that is meant to run offline.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport socket\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app_server import testing as app_testing\nfrom cli import testing as cli_testing\n\n\nclass NetworkAccessError(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"Raised when a test attempts to open a network connection.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _refuse_connection(*_args: object, **_kwargs: object) -> None:\n    raise NetworkAccessError(\"tests must not open network connections\")\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef _block_network(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> Iterator[None]:\n    monkeypatch.setattr(socket.socket, \"connect\", _refuse_connection)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(socket, \"create_connection\", _refuse_connection)\n    yield\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef project_root() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef cli_runner():\n    return cli_testing.cli_runner\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef web_client():\n    return app_testing.web_client()\n=== tests/test_load.py\n\"\"\"The `load` command: validates a file, stores its rates as text, reports the dates and rates counts.\n\nEach test runs the command in-process through `cli_runner` and reads the stored state back through\n`db.rates`. Every test shares one acceptance transaction with the command, which rolls back at the\nend, so the configured store is never left changed. Test currencies use the ZZ prefix so they never\ncollide with rates already in a store.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import parse_history\nfrom persistence import db as persistence_db\nfrom persistence.testing import db_session\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef rolled_back_transaction() -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Share one connection between the command and the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef build(header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write a file the way the ECB does: every line ends with a trailing comma.\"\"\"\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    writer = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    writer.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for row in rows:\n        writer.writerow(row + [\"\"])\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\n\ndef write(tmp_path: Path, name: str, text: str) -> str:\n    path = tmp_path / name\n    path.write_text(text, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    return str(path)\n\n\ndef stored(db, currency: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    return [(r.date, r.rate) for r in counts.\n\n`parse_history` checks the whole file before the first write, so a rejected file exits 3 and stores\nnothing. A file that cannot be opened or decoded exits 1 before any parsing or store access. Each rate is then written through the declared `rates.replace_rate` operation, which\nreplaces a rate already stored for the same date and currency, so loading a file twice leaves the\ndatabase unchanged.\n\nThe persistence library exposes no transaction operation, so each replace commits on its own. The\nvalidation above is what keeps a rejected file from changing anything; a store failure part way\nthrough a valid file is not rolled back.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sys\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import RejectedFile, parse_history\n\nOPERATIONAL_FAILURE = 1\nREJECTED = 3\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\n\n\ndef load(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Load the file named in `rest[0]` and return the exit code. The argument list is pre-validated.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0\n    try:\n        with open(rest[0], encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\") as handle:\n            text = handle.read()\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot read {rest[0]}: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        rates = parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile as error:\n        print(f\"error: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return REJECTED\n\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        for date, currency, rate in rates:\n            db.rates.replace_rate(date=date, currency=currency, rate=rate)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n\n    dates = {date for date, _, _ in rates}\n    print(\"dates,rates\")\n    print(f\"{len(dates)},{len(rates)}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nregister_command(\"load\", load)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":39,"oldLines":6,"newStart":39,"newLines":14,"lines":["         print(f\"error: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)","         return REJECTED"," ","+    return store_and_report(rates)","+","+","+def store_and_report(rates: list[tuple[str, str, str]]) -> int:","+    \"\"\"Store validated (date, currency, rate_text) rows and print the dates and rates counts.","+","+    Shared by `load` and `fetch`, so both commands store and report the same way.","+    \"\"\"","     db = open_store()","     try:","         for date, currency, rate in rates:"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_014PkjaE3ERKGuYujC3rUrvh","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgT2mG3f5wGiNgooXf7fw","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01BeWsbivqMhxTRpywcS35nw","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/cli/fetch_command.py","content":"\"\"\"The `fetch` command: download the ECB history archive, extract its CSV, and load it as `load` does.\n\nThe download is `fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive`, the single network call. It is looked up through\nits module at call time so tests replace that one seam. A failed download, bytes that are not a zip,\nor an archive without `eurofxref-hist.csv` exits 1 before any parsing. The extracted text then goes\nthrough the same `parse_history` validation and `store_and_report` path as `load`, so a rejected\nmember exits 3 and stores nothing.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport http.client\nimport io\nimport sys\nimport zipfile\nimport zlib\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom cli.load_command import store_and_report\nfrom fxrates_app import fetch\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import RejectedFile, parse_history\n\nOPERATIONAL_FAILURE = 1\nREJECTED = 3\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\nMEMBER_NAME = \"eurofxref-hist.csv\"\n\n\ndef fetch_history(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Download, extract, validate, and store the ECB history; return the exit code.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0\n    try:\n        archive = fetch.download_archive(fetch.ECB_ARCHIVE_URL)\n    except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot download {fetch.ECB_ARCHIVE_URL}: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(archive)) as zipped:\n            text = zipped.read(MEMBER_NAME).decode(\"utf-8\")\n    except (zipfile.BadZipFile, KeyError, UnicodeDecodeError, zlib.error) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot read {MEMBER_NAME} from the archive: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        rates = parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile as error:\n        print(f\"error: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return REJECTED\n\n    return store_and_report(rates)\n\n\nregister_command(\"fetch\", fetch_history)\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":409,"cache_read_input_tokens":46565,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":409},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"cb08b2e3-109d-4e7e-b122-fe6bd5fd3439","uuid":"253d2e35-fb95-4e74-9858-beb48181165a","timestamp":"2026-10-27T16:08:52.199Z","request_id":"req_011CgT2mFhKgi1hVdFPCupFd","wire_tool_inputs":{"toolu_01BeWsbivqMhxTRpywcS35nw":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/cli/fetch_command.py","content":"\"\"\"The `fetch` command: download the ECB history archive, extract its CSV, and load it as `load` does.\n\nThe download is `fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive`, the single network call. It is looked up through\nits module at call time so tests replace that one seam. A failed download, bytes that are not a zip,\nor an archive without `eurofxref-hist.csv` exits 1 before any parsing. The extracted text then goes\nthrough the same `parse_history` validation and `store_and_report` path as `load`, so a rejected\nmember exits 3 and stores nothing.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport http.client\nimport io\nimport sys\nimport zipfile\nimport zlib\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom cli.load_command import store_and_report\nfrom fxrates_app import fetch\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import RejectedFile, parse_history\n\nOPERATIONAL_FAILURE = 1\nREJECTED = 3\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\nMEMBER_NAME = \"eurofxref-hist.csv\"\n\n\ndef fetch_history(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Download, extract, validate, and store the ECB history; return the exit code.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0\n    try:\n        archive = fetch.download_archive(fetch.ECB_ARCHIVE_URL)\n    except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot download {fetch.ECB_ARCHIVE_URL}: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(archive)) as zipped:\n            text = zipped.read(MEMBER_NAME).decode(\"utf-8\")\n    except (zipfile.BadZipFile, KeyError, UnicodeDecodeError, zlib.error) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot read {MEMBER_NAME} from the archive: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        rates = parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile as error:\n        print(f\"error: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return REJECTED\n\n    return store_and_report(rates)\n\n\nregister_command(\"fetch\", fetch_history)\n"}}}

It is looked up through\nits module at call time so tests replace that one seam. A failed download, bytes that are not a zip,\nor an archive without `eurofxref-hist.csv` exits 1 before any parsing. The extracted text then goes\nthrough the same `parse_history` validation and `store_and_report` path as `load`, so a rejected\nmember exits 3 and stores nothing.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport http.client\nimport io\nimport sys\nimport zipfile\nimport zlib\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom cli.load_command import store_and_report\nfrom fxrates_app import fetch\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import RejectedFile, parse_history\n\nOPERATIONAL_FAILURE = 1\nREJECTED = 3\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\nMEMBER_NAME = \"eurofxref-hist.csv\"\n\n\ndef fetch_history(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Download, extract, validate, and store the ECB history; return the exit code.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return 0\n    try:\n        archive = fetch.download_archive(fetch.ECB_ARCHIVE_URL)\n    except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot download {fetch.ECB_ARCHIVE_URL}: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(archive)) as zipped:\n            text = zipped.read(MEMBER_NAME).decode(\"utf-8\")\n    except (zipfile.BadZipFile, KeyError, UnicodeDecodeError, zlib.error) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot read {MEMBER_NAME} from the archive: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        rates = parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile as error:\n        print(f\"error: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return REJECTED\n\n    return store_and_report(rates)\n\n\nregister_command(\"fetch\", fetch_history)\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01BeWsbivqMhxTRpywcS35nw","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport http.client\nimport io\nimport zipfile\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom fxrates_app import fetch\nfrom persistence import db as persistence_db\nfrom persistence.testing import db_session\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef rolled_back_transaction() -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Share one connection between the command and the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef csv_text(header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write CSV the way the ECB does: every line ends with a trailing comma.\"\"\"\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    writer = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    writer.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for row in rows:\n        writer.writerow(row + [\"\"])\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\n\ndef zip_with(member: str, text: str) -> bytes:\n    bio = io.BytesIO()\n    with zipfile.ZipFile(bio, \"w\") as z:\n        z.writestr(member, text)\n    return bio.getvalue()\n\n\ndef stored(db, currency: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    return [(r.date, r.rate) for r in db.rates.list_currency_history(currency=currency)]\n\n\ndef test_fetch_loads_archive(cli_runner) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-08-01\"\n    ra = \"1.50\"\n    rb = \"2.250\"\n    data = zip_with(\"eurofxref-hist.csv\", csv_text([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\", \"\"], [[d, ra, rb]]))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\", return_value=data):\n            code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\")\n        assert code == 0\n        lines = out.splitlines()\n        assert lines[0] == \"dates,rates\"\n        assert lines[1].split(\",\") == [str(1), str(2)]\n        rows = {r.currency: r.rate for r in db.rates.list_for_date(date=d)}\n        assert rows[\"ZZA\"] == ra\n        assert rows[\"ZZB\"] == rb\n\n\ndef test_fetch_download_failure(cli_runner) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-08-02\"\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        before = db.rates.list_all_keys()\n        with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\", side_effect=OSError(\"network down\")):\n            code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\")\n        assert code == 1\n        assert out == \"\"\n        assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n        assert db.rates.list_for_date(date=d) == []\n        assert len(db.rates.list_all_keys()) == len(before)\n\n\ndef test_fetch_bad_archive(cli_runner) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-08-03\"\n    wrong_member = zip_with(\"other.csv\", csv_text([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"\"], [[d, \"1.5\"]]))\n    not_a_zip = bytes(range(32))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        before = len(db.rates.list_all_keys())\n        for payload in (not_a_zip, wrong_member):\n            with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\", return_value=payload):\n                code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\")\n            assert code == 1\n            assert out == \"\"\n            assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n            assert db.rates.list_for_date(date=d) == []\n        assert len(db.rates.list_all_keys()) == before\n\n\ndef test_fetch_rejected_member(cli_runner) -> None:\n    good = \"1900-08-05\"\n    bad = \"1900-08-04\"\n    data = zip_with(\n        \"eurofxref-hist.csv\",\n        csv_text([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"\"], [[good, \"1.5\"], [bad, \"0\"]]),\n    )\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\", return_value=data):\n            code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\")\n        assert code == 3\n        assert out == \"\"\n        assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n        assert db.rates.list_for_date(date=good) == []\n        assert download.assert_called_once_with(\n        \"https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-hist.zip\"\n    )\n\n\ndef test_fetch_timeout_exits_one_and_stores_nothing(cli_runner) -> None:\n    with db_session() as db:\n        before = db.rates.list_all_keys()\n        with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\", side_effect=TimeoutError(\"timed out\")):\n            code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\")\n        assert code == 1\n        assert out == \"\"\n        assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n        assert db.rates.list_all_keys() == before\n\n\ndef test_fetch_protocol_error_exits_one(cli_runner) -> None:\n    with mock.patch(\n        \"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\",\n        side_effect=http.client.RemoteDisconnected(\"closed\"),\n    ):\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\")\n\n    assert code == 1\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n\n\ndef assert db.rates.list_all_keys() == before\n\n\ndef test_fetch_twice_reports_the_same_counts_and_leaves_rates_unchanged(cli_runner) -> None:\n    data = zip_with(\n        \"eurofxref-hist.csv\",\n Each test runs the command in-process through `cli_runner` and reads the stored state back\nthrough `db.rates`, inside one acceptance transaction that rolls back at the end.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport http.client\nimport io\nimport zipfile\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom fxrates_app import fetch\nfrom persistence import db as persistence_db\nfrom persistence.testing import db_session\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef rolled_back_transaction() -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Share one connection between the command and the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef csv_text(header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write CSV the way the ECB does: every line ends with a trailing comma.\"\"\"\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    writer = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    writer.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for row in rows:\n        writer.writerow(row + [\"\"])\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\n\ndef zip_with(member: str, text: str) -> bytes:\n    bio = io.BytesIO()\n    with zipfile.ZipFile(bio, \"w\") as z:\n        z.writestr(member, text)\n    return bio.getvalue()\n\n\ndef stored(db, currency: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    return [(r.date, r.rate) for r in db.rates.list_currency_history(currency=currency)]\n\n\ndef test_fetch_loads_archive(cli_runner) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-08-01\"\n    ra = \"1.50\"\n    rb = \"2.250\"\n    data = zip_with(\"eurofxref-hist.csv\", csv_text([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\", \"\"], [[d, ra, rb]]))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\", return_value=data):\n            code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\")\n        assert code == 0\n        lines = out.splitlines()\n        assert lines[0] == \"dates,rates\"\n        assert lines[1].split(\",\") == [str(1), str(2)]\n        rows = {r.currency: r.rate for r in           assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n            assert db.rates.list_for_date(date=d) == []\n        assert len(db.rates.list_all_keys()) == before\n\n\ndef Each test runs the command in-process through `cli_runner` and reads the stored state back\nthrough `db.rates`, inside one acceptance transaction that rolls back at the end.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport http.client\nimport io\nimport zipfile\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom fxrates_app import fetch\nfrom persistence import db as persistence_db\nfrom persistence.testing import db_session\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef rolled_back_transaction() -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Share one connection between the command and the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef csv_text(header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write CSV the way the ECB does: every line ends with a trailing comma.\"\"\"\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    writer = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    writer.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for row in rows:\n        writer.writerow(row + [\"\"])\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\n\ndef zip_with(member: str, text: str) -> bytes:\n    bio = io.BytesIO()\n    with zipfile.ZipFile(bio, \"w\") as z:\n        z.writestr(member, text)\n    return bio.getvalue()\n\n\ndef stored(db, currency: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    return [(r.date, r.rate) for r in db.rates.list_currency_history(currency=currency)]\n\n\ndef test_fetch_loads_archive(cli_runner) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-08-01\"\n    ra = \"1.50\"\n    rb = \"2.250\"\n    data = zip_with(\"eurofxref-hist.csv\", csv_text([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[d, ra, rb]]))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\", return_value=data):\n            code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\")\n        assert code == 0\n        lines = out.splitlines()\n        assert lines[0] == \"dates,rates\"\n        assert lines[1].split(\",\") == [str(1), str(2)]\n        rows = {r.currency: r.rate for r in db.rates.list_for_date(date=d)}\n        assert rows[\"ZZA\"] == ra\n        assert rows[\"ZZB\"] == rb\n\n\ndef test_fetch_download_failure(cli_runner) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-08-02\"\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        before = db.rates.list_all_keys()\n        with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\", side_effect=OSError(\"network down\")):\n            code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\")\n        assert code == 1\n        assert out == \"\"\n        assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n        assert db.rates.list_for_date(date=d) == []\n        assert len(db.rates.list_all_keys()) == len(before)\n\n\ndef test_fetch_bad_archive(cli_runner) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-08-03\"\n    wrong_member = zip_with(\"other.csv\", csv_text([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"\"], [[d, \"1.5\"]]))\n    not_a_zip = bytes(range(32))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        before = len(db.rates.list_all_keys())\n        for payload in (not_a_zip, wrong_member):\n            with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\", return_value=payload):\n                code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\")\n            assert code == 1\n            assert out == \"\"\n            assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n            assert db.rates.list_for_date(date=d) == []\n        assert len(db.rates.list_all_keys()) == before\n\n\ndef test_fetch_rejected_member(cli_runner) -> None:\n    good = \"1900-08-05\"\n    bad = \"1900-08-04\"\n    data = zip_with(\n        \"eurofxref-hist.csv\",\n        csv_text([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"\"], [[good, \"1.5\"], [bad, \"0\"]]),\n    )\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\", return_value=data):\n            code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\")\n        assert code == 3\n        assert out == \"\"\n        assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n        assert db.rates.list_for_date(date=good) == []\n        assert download.assert_called_once_with(\n        \"https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-hist.zip\"\n    )\n\n\ndef test_fetch_timeout_exits_one_and_stores_nothing(cli_runner) -> None:\n Each test runs the command in-process through `cli_runner` and reads the stored state back\nthrough `db.rates`, inside one acceptance transaction that rolls back at the end.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport http.client\nimport io\nimport zipfile\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom unittest import mock\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom fxrates_app import fetch\nfrom between the command and the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef csv_text(header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write CSV the way the ECB does: every line ends with a trailing comma.\"\"\"\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    writer = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    writer.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for row in rows:\n        writer.writerow(row + [\"\"])\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\n\ndef zip_with(member: str, text: str) -> bytes:\n    bio = io.BytesIO()\n    with zipfile.ZipFile(bio, \"w\") as z:\n        z.writestr(member, text)\n    return bio.getvalue()\n\n\ndef stored(db, currency: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    return [(r.date, r.rate) for r in db.rates.list_currency_history(currency=currency)]\n\n\ndef test_fetch_loads_archive(cli_runner) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-08-01\"\n    ra = \"1.50\"\n    rb = \"2.250\"\n    data = zip_with(\"eurofxref-hist.csv\", csv_text([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[d, ra, rb]]))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\", return_value=data):\n            code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\")\n        assert code == 0\n        lines = out.splitlines()\n        assert lines[0] == \"dates,rates\"\n        assert lines[1].split(\",\") == [str(1), str(2)]\n        rows = {r.currency: r.rate for r in db.rates.list_for_date(date=d)}\n        assert rows[\"ZZA\"] == ra\n        assert rows[\"ZZB\"] == rb\n\n\ndef test_fetch_download_failure(cli_runner) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-08-02\"\n\n    with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\", return_value=payload):\n                code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\")\n            assert code == 1\n            assert out == \"\"\n            assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n            assert db.rates.list_for_date(date=d) == []\n        assert len(db.rates.list_all_keys()) == before\n\n\ndef [[good, \"1.5\"], [bad, \"0\"]]),\n    )\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        with mock.patch(\"fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive\", return_value=data):\n            code, out, err = between the command and the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef csv_text(header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write CSV the way the ECB does: every line ends with a trailing comma.\"\"\"\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    writer = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    writer.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for row in rows:\n        writer.writerow(row + [\"\"])\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\n\ndef zip_with(member: str, text: str) -> bytes:\n    bio = io.BytesIO()\n    with zipfile.ZipFile(bio, \"w\") as z:\n        z.writestr(member, text)\n    return bio.getvalue()\n\n\ndef stored(db, currency: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    return [(r.date, r.rate) for r in db.rates.list_currency_history(currency=currency)]\n\n\ndef test_fetch_loads_archive(cli_runner) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-08-01\"\n    ra = \"1.50\"\n    rb = \"2.250\"\n    data = zip_with(\"eurofxref-hist.csv\", csv_text([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[d, == 0\n        lines = out.splitlines()\n        assert lines[0] == \"dates,rates\"\n        assert lines[1].split(\",\") == [str(1), str(2)]\n        rows = {r.currency: r.rate for r in
